sn12.24:1.1: [The Exalted One was once] staying near Rājagaha at the Bamboo Grove.
sn12.24:1.2: Now the venerable Sariputta clothed himself one morning, and taking his bowl and cloak entered Rājagaha on his alms round.
sn12.24:1.4: “It is too early as yet to go about Rājagaha for alms:
sn12.24:1.5: I might go to the gardens of the heretical Wanderers.”
sn12.24:2.1: Now the venerable Sariputta came to those gardens, and after exchanging greetings with those heretical Wanderers and compliments of friendship and courtesy,
sn12.24:2.2: sat down at one side. Then those Wanderers spoke thus to the venerable Sariputta so seated:
sn12.24:3.1: “There are, friend Sariputta, certain recluses and brahmins, believers in karma, who declare that ill is self-made;
sn12.24:3.2: certain others of them declare ill is made by someone other [than one’s self];
sn12.24:3.3: certain others declare that ill is made by both,
sn12.24:3.4: and certain others that ill is made by neither, but happens by chance.
sn12.24:3.5: But the recluse Gotama—what does he declare, what does he announce?
sn12.24:3.6: And how, if we were answering, should we be repeating the views of the recluse Gotama, and should not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct, but should be answering by a doctrine in conformity with his doctrine, and [one whereby] no one who is of his doctrine, a follower of his views, would render himself open to blame?”
sn12.24:4.1: “Friend, the Exalted One has said that ill comes to pass through a cause.
sn12.24:4.4: He who so spoke would be repeating the views of the Exalted One, and would not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct, but would be answering by a doctrine in conformity with his doctrine, and one whereby no one who is of his doctrine, a follower of his views, would render himself open to blame.
sn12.24:5.1: In the case of those recluses and brahmins, friend, who believing in karma declare that ill has been made by one’s own self, this ill was caused by contact.
sn12.24:5.2: In the case of those of them who declare that ill has been made by a different self, this ill too was caused by contact.
sn12.24:5.3: In the case of those of them who declare that ill has been made by both one’s own self and by a different self, this ill too was caused by contact.
sn12.24:5.4: In the case also of those who declare that ill has been made by neither, but has happened by chance, this ill too was caused by contact.
sn12.24:6.1: In no one of these four views of those who believe in karma is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins will experience feeling without contact.”
sn12.24:7.1: Now the venerable Ananda was listening to Sariputta’s talk with the heretical Wanderers.
sn12.24:7.2: And the venerable Ananda, after going his alms round in Rājagaha and eating his meal on his return, came into the presence of the Exalted One, saluted him, sat down at one side,
sn12.24:7.3: and so seated told the Exalted One what that talk had been, even all of it.
sn12.24:8.1: “Well done, well done, Ananda! Sariputta so answering would be answering rightly.
sn12.24:8.2: I have said that ill happens through a cause.
sn12.24:8.5: So saying one would be a repeater of my sayings; he would not be misrepresenting me by what is not correct, and no one who is of my doctrine, a follower of my views, would thereby render himself open to blame.
sn12.24:9.1: In each of the four cases, Ananda, of those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma, ill will have been caused by contact.
sn12.24:10.1: In no one of these four cases is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma will experience ill without contact.
sn12.24:11.1: I too, Ananda, was once staying here near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove at the Squirrels’ Feeding-ground.
sn12.24:11.4: I, too, finding it too early to make my alms round,
sn12.24:11.5: bethought me to go to the gardens of the heretical Wanderers.
sn12.24:12.1: They told me of those four views on karma and asked me,
sn12.24:12.2: What is the venerable Gotama’s view? What has he to announce to us? How answering, should we be repeating his views and should not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct?
sn12.24:13.1: And I answered them even as Sariputta answered.”
sn12.24:17.2: how the whole matter will have been said in one clause.
sn12.24:17.3: If this matter were spoken in detail, it were deep and it would seem deep.”
sn12.24:18.1: “Well then, Ananda, let just that reveal itself to you now.”
sn12.24:18.2: “If, lord, they were to ask me:—
sn12.24:18.3: ‘Decay-and-death, friend Ananda, what is its basis, what is its coming to pass, how is it brought to pass, what is its cause?’
sn12.24:18.5: ‘Decay-and-death, friends, is based on birth, through birth it comes to pass, is brought to pass, birth is its cause.’
sn12.24:19.1: Further, if they were to ask me the same concerning birth,
sn12.24:20.3: And I should answer further that
sn12.24:21.9: ‘And, friends, by the utter fading out and cessation of the six spheres of sense there is cessation of contact,
sn12.24:21.15: from this, cessation of decay-and-death, yea, grief, lamenting, ill, sorrow and despair cease.
sn12.24:21.16: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.24:21.17: So asked, lord, so should I make answer.”
